stories.headline: OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic to build a Claude-accelerated pretraining team

key_facts.fact: Andrej Karpathy, an OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla AI director, announced on Tuesday May 19, 2026 that he is joining Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Andrej Karpathy, an artificial intelligence researcher who co-founded OpenAI before getting poached by Tesla, announced on Tuesday that he's joining Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Karpathy posted on X: 'I've joined Anthropic. I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative. I am very excited to join the team here and get back to R&D.'
key_facts.excerpt: Personal update: I've joined Anthropic. I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative. I am very excited to join the team here and get back to R&D. I remain deeply passionate about education and plan to resume my work on it in time.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said Karpathy starts this week and will build a team focused on using Claude to accelerate pretraining research, working under head of pretraining Nick Joseph.
key_facts.excerpt: He will be working on pre-training under team lead Nick Joseph... Karpathy will start a team focused on using Claude to accelerate pre-training research.

key_facts.fact: The hire signals Anthropic believes AI-assisted research is its primary strategy for staying competitive with rivals like OpenAI and xAI in a market where talent has become as valuable as compute.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is betting that researchers like Karpathy can help push Claude further ahead in a market where talent has become just as valuable as compute, chips, and data centers.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Flash as its 'strongest agentic and coding model yet' at I/O 2026

key_facts.fact: At Google I/O on May 19, 2026, Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash, positioned as its strongest agentic and coding model, now the default model in the Gemini app and Search AI Mode globally.
key_facts.excerpt: Pichai said Gemini 3.5 Flash is 'remarkably fast.' The company said 3.5 Flash will now be the default model for the Gemini app and AI mode in search globally.

key_facts.fact: Gemini 3.5 Flash is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $9.00 per million output tokens (global), about 3x the per-token cost of the prior Gemini 3 Flash Preview.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 3.5 Flash | Input (text, image, video, audio) | $1.50 (Global) | Text output (response and reasoning) | $9.00 (Global)

key_facts.fact: Pichai said the model delivers frontier-level capability at less than half the price of comparable frontier models and runs four times faster on output tokens per second; he claimed top companies shifting 80% of workloads to 3.5 Flash could save over $1 billion a year.
key_facts.excerpt: If they shifted 80% of their workloads from other frontier models to 3.5 Flash, they'd save over $1 billion dollars annually... when looking at output tokens per second, it is four times faster than other frontier models.

key_facts.fact: On benchmarks, Gemini 3.5 Flash scored 76.2% on Terminal-bench 2.1 agentic terminal coding, 55.1% on SWE-Bench Pro, 83.6% on MCP Atlas, and 78.4% on OSWorld-Verified computer use.
key_facts.excerpt: Terminal-bench 2.1 | 76.2% | SWE-Bench Pro (Public) | 55.1% | MCP Atlas | 83.6% | OSWorld-Verified | 78.4%

key_facts.fact: Gemini 3.5 Pro, the heavier version, is being used internally at Google and will launch more broadly next month.
key_facts.excerpt: We're also excited for Gemini 3.5 Pro. We are using it internally, it's showing great improvements, and it will be coming next month.

stories.headline: Google unveils Gemini Omni, a world model that generates video from any input

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Gemini Omni at I/O 2026, a multimodal model 'capable of generating samples in any output modality from any input,' starting with video and combining Gemini's intelligence with Google's generative media models.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini Omni is our new model that is capable of generating samples in any output modality from any input. We're starting with video outputs, and over time we'll enable image and text.

key_facts.fact: The first model in the family, Gemini Omni Flash, is available starting today on the Gemini app, Google Flow and YouTube Shorts, with developer and enterprise API access coming in the following weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: The first model in the Omni family will be added to the Gemini app, Google Flow and YouTube Shorts. The new model will support output modalities like image and audio.

key_facts.fact: Omni lets users edit video conversationally and create a custom AI avatar that looks and sounds like them; Google said users must complete a dedicated onboarding to prevent deepfakes.
key_facts.excerpt: Users will also be able to create videos with their own digital avatars... users will have to undergo a dedicated product onboarding to prevent deepfakes.

key_facts.fact: Google framed Omni as part of its 'world model' push, moving AI from predicting text to simulating reality; a more advanced Omni Pro will follow with a claimed 'step change' in performance over Flash.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch is part of Google's next step in developing its own 'world model'... The more advanced version, Omni Pro, will be available when Google claims it offers a 'step change' in performance over Flash.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Guaranteed Capacity, selling 1-3 year compute commitments with volume discounts

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday May 19, 2026, OpenAI announced Guaranteed Capacity, letting customers secure long-term access to compute for products, agents and workflows via 1-, 2- or 3-year commitments with discounts that increase with annual commitment.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Tuesday announced a new offering called Guaranteed Capacity... customers can choose between one, two and three-year-long commitments, and it's offering discounts that increase based on those annual commitments.

key_facts.fact: Customers can draw down the committed spend across OpenAI's product portfolio and use guaranteed allocations across supported cloud providers and model families.
key_facts.excerpt: Customers can choose 1-3-year commitments, with discounts that increase based on annual commitment... customers can draw down from this commitment across the portfolio of OpenAI products.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman called it a 'big win-win' for planning ahead, said OpenAI will offer it until current allocation sells out, and that the company will ensure enough capacity remains for ChatGPT and Codex.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman said the new offering will help OpenAI plan ahead, which he hopes will be a 'big win-win.' He added that OpenAI will offer Guaranteed Capacity until it sells out of its current allocation... will make sure it leaves enough capacity available for its products like ChatGPT and its coding assistant Codex.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI positioned the offering as a way to help customers plan ahead 'in a compute-constrained world.'
key_facts.excerpt: Now, Guaranteed Capacity helps customers plan ahead for critical workloads in a compute-constrained world... we are offering discounted tokens for 1-3 year commits.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind to hire 20+ Contextual AI researchers in ~$90M licensing acqui-hire

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind agreed to hire more than 20 researchers from startup Contextual AI and license its technology, a source told Reuters on Tuesday May 19, 2026; the deal was first reported by Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Google DeepMind has paid up to $90 million to hire key researchers from Contextual AI, a move that has sparked increased scrutiny from antitrust regulators.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet paid between $80 million and $90 million to Contextual, and co-founder and CEO Douwe Kiela is among those moving to DeepMind.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet a versé entre 80 et 90 millions de dollars à Contextual dans le cadre de cet accord, et le cofondateur et directeur général de Contextual, Douwe Kiela, fait partie des personnes qui rejoignent DeepMind.

key_facts.fact: The deal is the latest licensing-style acqui-hire by Google's parent; last year it paid $2.4 billion in licensing fees to use AI coding startup Windsurf's technology and hire several key staff.
key_facts.excerpt: Im vergangenen Jahr zahlte das Unternehmen 2,4 Milliarden Dollar an Lizenzgebühren im Rahmen eines Deals zur Nutzung bestimmter Technologien des KI-Codegenerierungs-Startups Windsurf.

key_facts.fact: Such acqui-hire tactics, used to sidestep US antitrust review, have drawn regulatory scrutiny as a 'red flag'; Contextual AI raised an $80M Series A in 2024 led by Greycroft.
key_facts.excerpt: Les efforts déployés par les entreprises pour contourner le contrôle de la concurrence américain par des tactiques telles que les « acquihires » constituent un « signal d'alarme »... levé 80 millions de dollars lors d'un tour de table de série A en 2024, mené par Greycroft.

stories.headline: Sam Altman offers every YC startup $2M in OpenAI tokens in exchange for equity

key_facts.fact: Late Tuesday May 19, 2026, Sam Altman offered to invest $2 million in every startup in the current Y Combinator batch — paid not in cash but in OpenAI tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman late Tuesday offered to invest $2 million in every startup currently in the Y Combinator startup accelerator program—not in cash, but in OpenAI tokens.

key_facts.fact: Altman unveiled the offer in a talk to YC founders and posted on X: 'I am excited to see what will happen with tokenmaxxing startups, both for how they work internally and the products they can build.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'I am excited to see what will happen with tokenmaxxing startups, both for how they work internally and the products they can build,' Altman posted on X after unveiling the offer in a talk to YC founders.

key_facts.fact: The token investment gives early-stage AI startups cost-free access to advanced models for rapid prototyping while positioning OpenAI as both investor and infrastructure provider in the startup ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment positions OpenAI as both an investor and infrastructure provider, providing immediate advantages for early stage AI companies seeking to scale without upfront compute costs.

stories.headline: Two Nature papers show AI multi-agent systems succeed at validated drug-repurposing discoveries

key_facts.fact: Nature published two papers on May 19, 2026 describing AI multi-agent systems that help scientists generate and test hypotheses: Google's Co-Scientist and a system from FutureHouse.
key_facts.excerpt: Two papers have been published by Nature describing AI systems intended to help scientists develop and test hypotheses. One of the systems is called Co-Scientist... and another from FutureHouse.

key_facts.fact: Google's AI Co-Scientist proposed novel drug-repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that lab experiments validated, confirming the suggested drugs inhibit tumor viability at clinically relevant concentrations across multiple AML cell lines.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI co-scientist proposed novel repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Subsequent experiments validated these proposals, confirming that the suggested drugs inhibit tumor viability at clinically relevant concentrations in multiple AML cell lines.

key_facts.fact: FutureHouse's multi-agent system Robin identified ripasudil, a ROCK inhibitor used for glaucoma, as a novel candidate for dry age-related macular degeneration; the team built Robin and made the discovery in just 2.5 months.
key_facts.excerpt: We applied Robin to identify ripasudil, a Rho-kinase (ROCK) inhibitor clinically used to treat glaucoma, as a novel therapeutic candidate for dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD)... completed in just 2.5 months by a small team of researchers.

key_facts.fact: Both systems work in the background by orchestrating separate specialized tools and operate with expert-in-the-loop guidance across applications including drug repurposing, novel treatment targets, and antimicrobial resistance.
key_facts.excerpt: we evaluated end-to-end laboratory experiments probing the AI co-scientist-generated hypotheses and research proposals in three key biomedical applications: drug repurposing, proposing novel treatment targets, and elucidating the mechanisms underlying antimicrobial resistance. These settings all involved expert-in-the-loop guidance.
